patch.value: Plan mutations emit the complete step collection instead of a bounded changed-step receipt

During the 2026-09-28 ecosystem review, updating one field or status on the 15-step reconstruction plan emitted the full plan with all step bodies, linked items and resume context. Eight sequential update-step operations produced roughly 34902 tool-reported tokens of output. The mutation affects one step but response cost grows with the whole plan. This defeats the compact mutation default and agent tokens-per-completed-task goal. Preserve complete Plan functionality and explicit full inspection while making ordinary mutations cheap.

Public SDK owns an explicit compact Plan mutation receipt while CLI and MCP share its semantics; A 1000-step fixture proves a single-step update stays inside its declared output ceiling with no unrelated body text; Explicit full inspection still returns all steps decisions evidence and resume metadata with truthful omissions and continuation contracts; Completed planning-journey token replay includes mutation responses and fails when full-plan amplification is reintroduced

Default Plan mutation output contains plan/step identity, changed fields or counts, compact next action and an explicit route to full plan inspection, with output cost bounded independently of unrelated step bodies.
A one-step update on the live 15-step plan renders unrelated steps and lengthy resume context; repeated planning operations emitted tens of thousands of tokens.
